entries.languageReview: Sort out aims to resolve confusion; look into investigates without promising resolution.

entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Deal with means handle; solve guarantees a resolution more strongly.

entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Look into promises investigation; sort out promises an attempt at resolution.

entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Check on monitors welfare or status; check out explores or examines something of interest.

entries.languageReview: Check in with someone makes contact; check someone in registers their arrival.

entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Check out explores something; check on verifies its state or welfare.

entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Drop by suggests a brief casual visit; arrange a meeting suggests a planned appointment.

entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Pop in emphasises a quick informal visit; stay over includes an overnight stay.

entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Stop by suggests a brief visit; stop off explicitly emphasises a break along a journey.

entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Come round invites a visit toward the speaker; go round describes travelling to another person's home.

entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Head out focuses on leaving; arrive focuses on reaching the destination.
entries.pragmaticReview: head out: It is conversational and often signals imminent departure rather than a formal travel plan.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Set off starts a journey; get around describes travel within an area.
entries.pragmaticReview: set off: Set has the same form in present and past, so time words or context establish the tense.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Get around describes local mobility; set off describes starting a journey.
entries.pragmaticReview: get around: Ask about accessibility and distances rather than assuming one transport option suits everyone.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Pick up collects; drop off delivers and leaves someone or something.

entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Drop off delivers; pick up collects.
entries.pragmaticReview: drop off: The visit may be very brief; clarify if you also need the person to wait or help inside.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Run out of says none remains; run low on says a small amount remains.

entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Stock up buys a reserve; top up replenishes an existing amount.

entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Use up emphasises total consumption; use alone does not imply exhaustion.

entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Wear out concerns loss of usefulness through use; wear off often describes an effect gradually disappearing.
entries.pragmaticReview: wear out: It suggests cumulative use, whereas break may describe a sudden failure.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Break down stops a machine working; wear out describes deterioration through use.
entries.pragmaticReview: break down: The past tense is broke down; broken down is used with has or had.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Act up informally describes unreliable operation; break down suggests a more definite failure.

entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Put aside reserves resources; spend uses them for a current purpose.

entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Save up stresses gradual accumulation toward a goal; put aside stresses reserving an amount.

entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Pay back returns borrowed money; pay for covers the cost of goods or services.

entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Split the bill means share payment; the division need not be equal.

entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Chip in contributes to a shared effort; pay back repays a debt.

entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Cut down on reduces; cut out removes entirely.
entries.pragmaticReview: cut down on: State the amount or habit you want to reduce so progress is observable.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Stick to follows a commitment; stick with can mean continue using or supporting something.

entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Get used to describes adaptation; used to plus a verb describes a past habit.

entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Look forward to expresses positive anticipation; expect simply predicts.

entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Feel up to concerns energy or readiness; be up for concerns willingness or interest.

entries.languageReview: Be up for expresses willingness; feel up to emphasises sufficient energy.

entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Keen on takes a noun or -ing form; keen to takes an infinitive.

entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Be into describes interest; get into describes developing that interest.
entries.pragmaticReview: be into: Informal; interested in is safer in formal introductions or reports.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Tied up means temporarily unavailable; snowed under suggests an excessive workload.

entries.languageReview: Snowed under suggests being overwhelmed; busy can describe a manageable workload.
entries.pragmaticReview: be snowed under: It is an informal exaggeration, not a measured workload report; add numbers when requesting resources.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Stretched thin divides limited capacity among many demands; tied up describes temporary unavailability.

entries.languageReview: Make time for deliberately prioritises; have time for merely states availability.

entries.languageReview: Squeeze in stresses limited space or time; fit in can sound less pressured.

entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Put someone up provides accommodation; put up with tolerates something.

entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Stay over includes an overnight stay; drop by usually means a brief visit.
entries.pragmaticReview: stay over: Confirm practical details such as timing and sleeping arrangements rather than assuming an invitation covers them.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Show around guides a visitor through a place; explain describes it without necessarily moving through it.

entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Help out suggests practical assistance in a need; take over assumes responsibility or control.

entries.languageReview: Count on expresses confident expectation; hope for expresses a wish without the same assurance.

entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Rely on emphasises dependence; count on often emphasises confident expectation.

entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Makes sense means understandable or logical; is true asserts factual correctness.

entries.languageReview: Fair enough accepts a position as reasonable; excellent expresses strong approval.

entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Relief is the noun; relieve is the verb describing removal of worry or discomfort.

entries.languageReview: What a shame expresses disappointment; shame on you condemns someone's behaviour.

entries.languageReview: How come keeps statement word order; why normally uses question inversion.

entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: That explains it signals a newly understood cause; I thought as much confirms a prior suspicion.

entries.languageReview: This acknowledges practical difficulty; impossible rules out success entirely.

entries.languageReview: The phrase reassures about a manageable problem; it does not mean the problem has no impact.

entries.languageReview: One thing at a time sets sequential focus; all at once attempts simultaneous action.

entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.
